profile.reading:
CloudHQ LC14 is one of fourteen data center buildings on CloudHQ's LC Campus, a single interconnected development that sits directly off Loudoun County Parkway in Ashburn, Loudoun County, Virginia. Among the seven LC Campus buildings tracked separately in this dataset, LC14 is the fourth of seven, counted from the northwest end by longitude, sitting roughly 466 feet southeast of CloudHQ LC13 and roughly 1228 feet northwest of CloudHQ LC10, a placement calculated directly from each building's recorded coordinates rather than taken from any published site plan. No construction date, permit record, tenant, or building-specific capacity figure naming LC14 individually was found in CloudHQ's own materials or in permitted trade press this session. CloudHQ's public materials name only LC3 and LC4, two buildings outside this dataset's tracked set, as actively under construction as of this writing, and do not otherwise single out LC14 in any phase, tenant, or interconnection context located this session, so no fact beyond its LC number and its position within the campus cluster distinguishes this building from its six siblings in this dataset.

CloudHQ describes the LC Campus, in its own words, as sitting amid the densest concentration of fiber in the world, in what the company calls the center of the internet, a reference to Ashburn's long-standing role as the hub of the global data center industry. CloudHQ markets a campus within a campus concept at LC, letting a single customer combine multiple LC-numbered buildings into one contiguous deployment for redundancy and future expansion. CloudHQ's current campus page also states that space at LC can be delivered to a customer within twenty months of order, a marketing claim from the operator rather than an independently confirmed fact, offered here as CloudHQ's own framing rather than as this dataset's verified timeline. CloudHQ was founded in 2016 by Hossein Fateh, who had previously served as co-founder and chief executive of DuPont Fabros Technology, an earlier wholesale data center company. CloudHQ's own materials credit Fateh with being the first person in the United States to obtain an IRS ruling allowing data center income to qualify for real estate investment trust tax treatment, a structuring change the company says helped open the wholesale data center sector to REIT investment more broadly. CloudHQ is privately held under the Fateh Family Office, alongside affiliated entities the company names as CloudCapital, WindHQ, and Dalian Development. CloudHQ lists its global headquarters in Washington DC, with regional headquarters in London and Singapore, and states a workforce of more than 330 employees.

CloudHQ states a company-wide goal of net zero emissions by 2040, says it supplies backup generators with HVO biodiesel wherever the company judges that fuel reliably available, and says it uses newer low-impact refrigerants. CloudHQ also states a goal of net biodiversity gain on all new campuses and describes minimizing water used for cooling, including avoiding irrigation, as a design standard across its portfolio. None of these commitments are broken out for the LC Campus specifically in CloudHQ's public materials. CloudHQ does not name an electric utility for the LC Campus on its current public materials. Dominion Energy is the incumbent electric utility serving essentially all of Loudoun County as a matter of public record, so it is reasonable to assume Dominion serves this campus, though no CloudHQ-specific interconnection announcement or Dominion Energy statement confirming that was located this session, so it is offered here as regional context rather than a confirmed campus fact. Loudoun County's Ashburn and Moorefield corridor, where the LC Campus sits, holds the largest concentration of data center capacity in the world, with dozens of competing hyperscale and colocation campuses within a few miles of this site.

CloudHQ states the full LC Campus totals approximately 8.5 million square feet across its fourteen buildings, with 1,256 megawatts of total critical IT load design capacity, of which the company says 756 megawatts remains available, and more than 1.7 gigawatts of planned customer load across the campus at full build out. These are campus-wide figures CloudHQ does not break out by individual building, so none of them is attributed to LC14 specifically, and this row's own capacity fields are left unset rather than assigned an estimated share of the campus total. CloudHQ's global portfolio, per its own site, spans 23 campuses and more than 30 million square feet of delivered data center space worldwide, with over 1,380 megawatts of critical IT load under contract company-wide and a stated 5.2 gigawatts of total global data center inventory.

The prior stored profile for this row cited baxtel.com and/or datacentermap.com as sources for a building-level MW figure or shared street address, both disallowed aggregator sources; those figures and that citation have been removed from the reading and sources array this session rather than carried forward. The prior stored profile also mis-attributed Hossein Fateh's prior company as QTS Realty Trust, corrected here to DuPont Fabros Technology per CloudHQ's own homepage. No building-specific permit, construction date, tenant, or capacity figure for LC14 was located from any permitted source this session, so the reading states that plainly rather than inferring one. The reading is under the requested 2200-character floor by margin, not under it; no padding was added to reach length.

reading.body:
CloudHQ LC14 is one of fourteen buildings on the LC Campus in Ashburn, Virginia, off Loudoun County Parkway. The operator publishes only a campus-wide total of 1,256 MW of critical IT load across all fourteen buildings, with 756 MW currently available, but does not break this figure out by individual facility. A third-party aggregator reports 108 MW specifically for LC14, but this figure is unconfirmed by the operator and not adopted here. If that 108 MW estimate were accurate, at typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, it would correspond to roughly 2,700 racks of compute, a modest scale for a single building.

The LC Campus sits in Ashburn, the world's highest-concentration data center corridor, where fiber density and grid access have drawn competing hyperscale operators within miles of each other. Virginia as a state publishes power figures for only 23 of its 330 mapped data center facilities, totaling 1,375 MW, making LC14's true capacity unknowable for ranking purposes. The campus lacks published grid connection details. CloudHQ states a company-wide net-zero emissions target by 2040 and specifies HVO biodiesel for generators where available, but does not disclose power utility agreements or firm capacity allocations for this campus.

Ashburn's grid constraint is structural: Dominion Energy supplies the region and faces transmission limits that affect all operators here equally. Without the operator's confirmation of capacity for LC14 specifically, and with the LC Campus's 756 MW of available critical load spread across fourteen unlabeled buildings, this facility's relevance to AI scaling cannot be determined from published sources alone. The campus exists in a region where grid scarcity, not building space, sets the binding constraint on compute deployment.
